posts.author: Andrej Karpathy
posts.text: Don't think of LLMs as entities but as simulators. For example, when exploring a topic, don't ask: "What do you think about xyz"? There is no "you". Next time try: "What would be a good group of people to explore xyz? Wh…
posts.summary: Andrej Karpathy suggests thinking of LLMs as simulators rather than entities with their own opinions. He recommends prompting them to simulate specific perspectives rather than asking for their personal view.

posts.author: Aakash Gupta
posts.text: Everyone assumes ChatGPT’s memory is some sophisticated RAG system with vector databases and semantic search. Manthan reverse engineered it. The actual architecture is almost disappointingly simple: session metadata that…
posts.summary: Aakash Gupta discusses how ChatGPT's memory architecture relies on a simple combination of session metadata, stored facts, lightweight summaries, and a sliding window rather than a complex RAG system.

posts.author: Boris Cherny
posts.text: Something I have been thinking about: in the past, the best engineers I knew spent a lot of time automating their work in various ways. Better vim/emacs automations, writing lint rules to catch repeat code issues, buildi…
posts.summary: Boris Cherny argues that engineering automation, such as lint rules and CI tests, has become even more critical with AI agents to encode domain knowledge and multiply team output. He suggests that teams must document rules and workflows in files like CLAUDE.md so that AI agents and new contributors can work effectively.

posts.author: Santiago
posts.text: Day 1: You don't know how to use abstractions, so you write flat code. Day 1000: Your code is fancier and full of abstractions. It's "flexible", "scalable", "observable", and a bunch of other "-able". Day 3000: You reali…
posts.summary: The author observes that software engineers evolve from writing flat code to over-engineering with complex abstractions, and eventually return to writing flat code after realizing the pitfalls of over-engineering.

posts.author: Theo - t3.gg
posts.text: If you understand your whole codebase, the codebase isn't that important. Real software is larger than what your brain can comprehend.
posts.summary: The author argues that if a developer fully understands a codebase, its size becomes less of a barrier. They emphasize that real-world software is often too large for a single human brain to comprehend entirely.

posts.author: Paul Graham

posts.summary: Paul Graham shares advice given to a 14-year-old about shifting focus to game management, such as getting enough sleep and staying calm, once exam preparation is complete.
